parole.significato: open, wide (featuring a very large open area, especially sea)
parole.testo: Unknown. Possibly a variant of aapa (with leveling of the weak grade aava-, influenced perhaps by avata), or a separate Sami borrowing (from Proto-Samic *āvõs).

parole.significato: a humid or damp forest or grove, usually one by a river
parole.testo: From a Sami language, compare Northern Sami ávžu, from Proto-Samic *āvčō.

parole.significato: a large herd of reindeer, often thousands of reindeer
parole.testo: From a Sami language (compare Northern Sami eallu), ultimately from Proto-Samic *ealō.

parole.significato: type of swamp; free of, or sparsely covered by trees, especially in northern Finland (such as Lapland and Kainuu)
parole.testo: From a Sami language, ultimately from Proto-Samic *jeaŋkē (compare Northern Sami jeaggi).

parole.significato: gas (state of matter)
parole.testo: Borrowed from a Sami language (compare Southern Sami gaasoe (“cold mist”)), from Proto-Samic *kāsō, from Proto-Uralic *käsä (“dew”). Originally a dialectal word meaning “(cold) mist, fog”, adopted as an equivalent of gas by Finnish physician and author Samuel Roos in 1845, by phonetic similarity wit

parole.significato: to wade, ford (walk through water, snow or something else that impedes progress)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Sami, from Proto-Samic *kālētēk, ultimately from Proto-Uralic *kälä- (whence also Erzya келямс (keľams, “to ford”)).

parole.significato: large wilderness between rivers in northern Finland
parole.testo: From a Sami language, compare Northern Sami skáidi (“land between rivers, cape”), from Proto-Samic *skājδē.

parole.significato: spring (place where water emerges to the surface)
parole.testo: Borrowed via Sami (compare Southern Sami gaaltije), from Proto-Samic *kāltëjō, itself borrowed from Proto-Germanic *kaldijǭ (whence Old Norse kelda, Norwegian kjelde, Swedish källa).

parole.significato: means, way, vehicle (entity to achieve an end)
parole.testo: Probably borrowed from Sami, from Proto-Samic *keajnō (“road”). Cognate with Karelian keino.

parole.significato: A round, treeless top of a fell.
parole.testo: Borrowing from Sami, compare Northern Sami čearru, from Proto-Samic *čearō.

parole.significato: A resting hole in snow dug by a bird or an arctic fox.
parole.testo: From Sami, ultimately from Proto-Samic *čieppë.

parole.significato: a small box or chest with a lid
parole.testo: Borrowed from a Sami language (compare Northern Sami giisá), ultimately from Proto-Samic *kijsā.

parole.significato: a hoof, especially of a reindeer
parole.testo: Borrowed from Sami language, from Proto-Samic *kuopērē.

parole.significato: a heavy seine used in flowing water, such as a river
parole.testo: kultaa + -e; the root is a dialectal verb meaning "to catch or touch something in water or a liquid", itself borrowed from Sami (compare Northern Sami goldit), from Proto-Samic *koltētēk.

parole.significato: a mossy and humid boreal forest
parole.testo: From Sami, compare Skolt Sami kuõlbân, from Proto-Samic *kuolpën.

parole.significato: waterfall, rapids
parole.testo: From Sami, compare Inari Sami korže, from Proto-Samic *korčē.

parole.significato: reindeer botfly (Hypoderma tarandi)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Sami (compare Northern Sami gurbmá), ultimately from Proto-Samic *kurmā.

parole.significato: glen, dale, ravine, valley
parole.testo: Borrowed from Sami (compare Northern Sami gorsa), from Proto-Samic *korsë. Doublet of kuru.

parole.significato: A steep, foamy waterfall, a cascade.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Sami (compare Northern Sami geavŋŋis), ultimately from Proto-Samic *keavŋēs.

parole.significato: lean-to (type of shelter with a diagonal roof and open on one side)
parole.testo: Borrowed from a Sami language, compare Northern Sami lávvu, ultimately from Proto-Samic *lāvō.

parole.significato: The parts of Finland south of Sápmi.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Sami (compare Northern Sami láddi), from Proto-Samic *lāntē, from North Germanic (compare Swedish land).

parole.significato: a sleeping place or bed, either temporary or in a kota
parole.testo: Borrowed from Sami, compare Northern Sami loaidu, ultimately from Proto-Samic *loajtō.

parole.significato: a wide stream pool in a river or a small lake through which a river passes
parole.testo: From a Sami language, compare Northern Sami luoppal, from Proto-Samic *luompël. Ultimately related to lampi.

parole.significato: beard-like lichen that typically grow on trees, of the genera Bryoria and Bryoria
parole.testo: ] Probably borrowed from Sami, from Proto-Samic *loppō ~ *lëppō.

parole.significato: synonym of joenniska
parole.testo: From Sami (compare Northern Sami lusmi), from Proto-Samic *lusmē.

parole.significato: synonym of kannas (“isthmus”)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Sami (compare Northern Sami muotki), from Proto-Samic *muotkē. Doublet of matka.

parole.significato: walrus, Odobenus rosmarus
parole.testo: From a Sami language, compare Northern Sami morša, ultimately from Proto-Samic *moršë.

parole.significato: A small rapid in a river.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Sami; compare Northern Sami njavvi (“small rapid, small river”), from Proto-Samic *ńëvē.

parole.significato: packing snow (wet, sticky snow that is suitable for making snowmen etc.)
parole.testo: Borrowed from a Sami language, from Proto-Samic *ńuockës, from Proto-Finno-Ugric *ńëčke.

parole.significato: campfire, fire (open fire, for example for cooking or heating)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Sami (compare Inari Sami njuáržu), ultimately from Proto-Samic *ńuodšō; possibly originally a substrate word.

parole.significato: a traditional fur boot of the Sami people, sewed by hand of reindeer leg skin; (in the plural) a pair of these boots
parole.testo: Borrowed from Sami + -kas (compare Northern Sami nuvttot; Lule Sami nuvtaga; Southern Sami novhtehke; Kildin Sami пиматҍ (pimat'); Skolt Sami nuˈtrneǩ; Inari Sami njuuppâh; Ume Sami nuuhtahka), from a Proto-Samic *nuvttVkke̮ or *nuttVkke̮. Sámi synonyms includes variants of: Northern Sami gállohat,

parole.significato: naled, aufeis (sheet-like ice)
parole.testo: From a Sami language (compare Southern Sami baadtehts (“sheet-ice”)), ultimately from Proto-Samic *pāntëtēk.

parole.significato: to wander in herds over the summer
parole.testo: Borrowed from Sami (compare Northern Sami bálgat), ultimately from Proto-Samic *pālkëtēk.

parole.significato: halibut
parole.testo: From a Sami language, compare Northern Sami bálddis, ultimately from Proto-Samic *pāltēs

parole.significato: A type of reindeer fur coat.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Sami, ultimately from Proto-Samic *peackë.

parole.significato: In a kota (Sami tipi-like dwelling), an area opposite to the door opening, reserved for storage of kitchen utensils and…
parole.testo: From a Sami language (compare Northern Sami boaššu), ultimately from Proto-Samic *poaššō. Doublet of pohja (inherited from Finnic).

parole.significato: moult (the loss of summer fur by an animal before the winter; used at least of reindeer)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Sami (compare Northern Sami borgi), from Proto-Samic *porkē.

parole.significato: In a ski, the place on which the foot is supported.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Sami (whence Northern Sami beađŋŋis, from Proto-Samic *peaδŋēs).

parole.significato: to fiddle, pick
parole.testo: Probably borrowed from Sami (from Proto-Samic *roŋkëtēk, compare Northern Sami roggat). Cognate with Karelian ronkkie.

parole.significato: forested esker
parole.testo: Borrowed from Sami, from Proto-Samic *roavē.

parole.significato: stag, adult male reindeer
parole.testo: Borrowed from Sami (compare Northern Sami sarvvis), from Proto-Samic *sërvēs. Doublet of hirvas.

parole.significato: sieidi (a Sami sacred place)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Sami, compare Northern Sami sieidi, from Proto-Samic *siejtē.

parole.significato: A rim in the lower part of a ski pole that prevents it from sinking too deep; a basket.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Sami, compare Proto-Samic *soampē, Northern Sami soabbi, in turn from Proto-Indo-European *stombʰos. Doublet with sammas.

parole.significato: to suit up, clothe, dress up
parole.testo: sontu- + -ustaa, derived from the obsolete dialectal noun sonnus (“hem”) (with + -taa); or directly from dialectal sontu (“inside of leather”), probably a Sami borrowing (compare Northern Sami cuozza), ultimately from Proto-Samic *cuoncë.

parole.significato: A type of lasso used to catch reindeer.
parole.testo: From a Sami language, from Proto-Samic *suoppënjë.

parole.significato: to leak (of a container), seep (out of a shoe, wooden container, etc.)
parole.testo: Probably borrowed from Sami, from Proto-Samic *suoδëtēk; compare Southern Sami soeredh (“to leak, to seep”), Northern Sami suođđat (“to hiss, to leak (air)”).

parole.significato: brown trout (Salmo trutta morph fario, Salmo trutta morph lacustris)
parole.testo: From a Sami language, compare Lule Sami dábmuk, Proto-Samic *tāmmukkë.

parole.significato: fell; a mountain belonging to the Scandinavian Mountains or otherwise located in or around Northern Finland or, less co…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Sami, compare Kildin Sami тӯнтар (tūntar), from Proto-Samic *tuontër. Doublet of tanner, tantere, and tundra.

parole.significato: whale
parole.testo: Borrowed from a Sami language, from Proto-Samic *fālēs (compare Northern Sami fális), from Proto-Germanic *hwalaz (“whale”). Originally more commonly used as a part of the compound valaskala, for which compare Swedish valfisk.

parole.significato: disgusting, nasty
parole.testo: Borrowed from Sami (compare Northern Sami fasti), ultimately from Proto-Samic *vëstē.

parole.significato: freshly fallen white and dry snow
parole.testo: Borrowing from a Sami language, from Proto-Samic *vëcë. Compare Northern Sami vahca.

parole.significato: a rope used to pull a toboggan, sled, pulk or reindeer harness
parole.testo: Borrowed from a Sami language, ultimately from Proto-Samic *vuotërājppē.

parole.significato: navigable waterway, especially through a body of water
parole.testo: Probably borrowed from a Sami language, from Proto-Samic *vāvlē.

parole.significato: astonished (used chiefly idiomatically in the expression olla äimänä (“to be astonished”), and as root of derived terms)
parole.testo: Probably borrowed from Sami, from Proto-Samic *eajmē.
